calls.reason: ETR's survey of 600 technology leaders found half reported AI value exceeding cost. Although self-reported, that substantially undercuts the near-universal claim; KPMG establishes widespread difficulties, not universality.

NVIDIA's filing confirms three direct customers supplied 54% of revenue, but distinguishes purchasers from downstream users. It does not establish unsustainable demand, and industry health remains a judgment.
Sightline documents construction delays and Anthropic's filing shows losses. Neither establishes the compute or combined backlog shares, and the packet does not demonstrate misleading accounting.

The Decoder reports uncertain Anthropic cost estimates; Altman's admission establishes earlier OpenAI subscription losses. Tom's Hardware measures API-equivalent value, leaving actual heavy-user costs at both companies unresolved.

Anthropic's filing shows costs growing slower than revenue, while WIRED confirms temporary reduced fees. The savings are unspecified, so the evidence cannot establish whether those concessions alone produced Q2 profit.
